mainTopic: How much work may be done on שבת when it is permitted: the עומר's three סאה, an extra slaughtered offering, intention versus action, and picking figs for a sick person.
overview: Our משנה has רבי ישמעאל saying the עומר came from five סאה of barley on a weekday but only three on שבת, while the חכמים say three in both cases. The גמרא looks for another sage who shares רבי ישמעאל's idea. It tries רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, then רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים (one reaper on שבת), then רבי יוסי (witnesses of a clearly seen new moon do not travel on שבת). Each comparison rests on the idea כיון דאפשר לא טרחינן: if less work will do, we don't do extra on שבת. Each comparison is pushed away, because the cases differ. Next comes a ruling about someone who slaughtered two communal חטאות on שבת when only one was needed. A contradiction in רבה's words is resolved. רבינא then asks whether we judge by a person's intention or by what actually happened, and רב אשי answers with two versions based on the case of a net that caught fish and a drowning child. The amud ends with רבה's ruling that everyone who picks figs for a sick person on שבת is exempt. רבא then asks whether to pick two figs on two stems or three on one stem, and the גמרא begins to answer that we bring the three.

steps.title: Maybe רבי ישמעאל holds like the רבנן on the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the earlier comparison. Our רבי ישמעאל may agree with the רבנן, who say the whole קרבן פסח is skinned even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: I can tell you he holds like the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the earlier idea that our רבי ישמעאל follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא. It says he might hold like the רבנן instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier suggestion linked two rulings about cutting back work on שבת. This step says there is no proof of that link. Our רבי ישמעאל could hold like the רבנן on the פסח question and still say three סאה for the עומר on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the Rabbis, meaning the majority view against the individual sage
He holds, meaning this is his opinion
I can say to you. A way of showing another explanation is possible

phrases.english: I can say to you
that he holds like the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: "He" is our רבי ישמעאל. The רבנן here say the whole קרבן פסח is skinned even on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא לָךְ כְּרַבָּנַן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made just before this section, which linked רבי ישמעאל to רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that our רבי ישמעאל must follow רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא on skinning the פסח.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is no proof of the link. Our רבי ישמעאל could hold like the רבנן on the פסח question.

steps.title: Even רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא might agree in the case of the עומר
steps.stepSummary: A second rejection. Even the son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא may have been lenient only for the פסח. There, the needed Temple service was already done. For the עומר, the service is not yet complete, so he might agree with the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively, רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא only said his ruling there, where the needs of the Most High were already taken care of and there is no need to break שבת. But here, where the needs of the Most High were not taken care of and one must break שבת, say he holds like the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second reason the comparison fails. The two cases are different, so even the son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא might not be lenient for the עומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסח case, the Temple's need was already met, so skinning the rest would be extra work on שבת with no purpose. With the עומר, the Temple's need, a proper high-quality offering, is not yet met, and the work on שבת is needed for it. So there he may agree we do the full amount, like the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively, introducing a second answer
He only said it here. A way of limiting a ruling to its own case
The need of the Most High, meaning what the Temple service requires
To desecrate שבת, meaning doing work that is normally forbidden on שבת

phrases.english: Alternatively,
[he] only stated [his ruling]

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם, אֶלָּא דְּאִיתְעֲבִיד לֵיהּ צוֹרֶךְ גָּבוֹהַּ,
phrases.english: there, where the need of the Most High has been done,
phrases.notes: "There" is the קרבן פסח on שבת. Once it is skinned to the chest, what the Temple needs is already done.

phrases.english: and there is no need to desecrate Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּלָא אִיתְעֲבִיד לֵיהּ צוֹרֶךְ גָּבוֹהַּ,
phrases.english: but here, where the need of the Most High has not been done,
phrases.notes: "Here" is the עומר. With fewer סאה, the high-quality flour the Temple needs might not be ready.

phrases.english: and it is necessary to desecrate Shabbat –
say that he holds like the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי, עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, stronger rejection of the same comparison by showing the two cases are different.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the leniency for skinning the פסח carries over to the amount of barley for the עומר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: For the פסח, the Temple's need was already met, so the extra work had no purpose. For the עומר, the need is not yet met and the work is needed.

steps.title: רבה offers a new comparison: רבי ישמעאל and רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים
steps.stepSummary: רבה drops the first comparison. He says רבי ישמעאל shares the view of רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה said: רבי ישמעאל and רבי חנינא the deputy of the priests said the same thing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה brings a new explanation for רבי ישמעאל's view. This sets up the next step, where the source for רבי חנינא is quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the first comparison failed, רבה looks for a sage whose view is also about the עומר itself. That makes the match much closer than the פסח case.

keyTerms.meaning: The deputy of the כהנים, second to the כהן גדול
One thing, meaning the same idea
Rather. Shows the earlier approach is dropped and a new one begins

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא סְגַן הַכֹּהֲנִים
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Chanina the deputy High Priest
said the same thing,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבָּה: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא סְגַן הַכֹּהֲנִים אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected comparison with a new one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל's view on the עומר on שבת matches the view of רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים.

steps.title: The משנה of רבי חנינא: on שבת the barley is cut by one person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. רבי חנינא says on שבת the עומר barley is cut by one person with one sickle and one basket, and on a weekday by three. The חכמים say three on both days.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים says: On שבת it is cut by one person, with one sickle and one basket. On a weekday it is cut by three, with three baskets and three sickles. The חכמים say: both on שבת and on a weekday, with three baskets and three sickles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source behind רבה's comparison. This is a dispute about how the עומר barley is cut on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The setup matches our משנה exactly. רבי חנינא reduces the work on שבת, and the חכמים say do the same as on a weekday. Our משנה has the same pattern: רבי ישמעאל reduces from five סאה to three, and the חכמים do not.

keyTerms.meaning: Is cut or harvested
By one person
Sickle
Basket
A weekday, not שבת or יום טוב

phrases.english: As we learned in the Mishna:
Rabbi Chanina the deputy High Priest says:
On Shabbat it is reaped by one person,
phrases.notes: "It" is the barley for the עומר.

phrases.english: with one sickle and with one basket,
and on a weekday – by three,
with three baskets and with three sickles.
And the Sages say:
both on Shabbat and on a weekday –
with three baskets and with three sickles.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא סְגַן הַכֹּהֲנִים אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source that רבה's comparison is built on.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's claim that רבי ישמעאל and רבי חנינא hold the same idea.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה where רבי חנינא says that on שבת the עומר is cut by one person with one sickle and one basket.

steps.title: The shared idea: if less is possible, we don't do extra on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the link. רבי חנינא holds that since one person can do the cutting, we don't add more work on שבת. רבי ישמעאל holds the same about using three סאה instead of five.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't רבי חנינא the deputy of the priests say there that since it is possible, we don't go to extra effort? Here too, since it is possible, we don't go to extra effort.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the one principle behind both rulings. If the job can be done with less work on שבת, we don't do more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי חנינא, one person reaping is enough, so three is unnecessary effort on שבת. For רבי ישמעאל, an עומר can be made from three סאה, so cutting five on שבת is unnecessary effort. This explains רבי ישמעאל's view through a case about the עומר itself, which is closer than the פסח comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't he? A question used to make a point the listener should agree with
Since it is possible, meaning there is a way to manage with less
We don't go to extra effort

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's proposal rests on the rule כיון דאפשר לא טרחינן: on שבת, if the עומר can be made with less work (three סאה, like one reaper for רבי חנינא), we don't do the extra. Steps 6 and 7 reject this comparison.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a clear general idea: on שבת, even work that is allowed for the Temple should be kept to what is truly needed.

phrases.english: Doesn't he say
Rabbi Chanina the deputy High Priest there,
since it is possible – we do not exert ourselves,
phrases.notes: Since one person can do the cutting, we don't bring three on שבת.

phrases.english: here too,
since it is possible – we do not exert ourselves.
phrases.notes: Since an עומר can come from three סאה, we don't cut five on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא סְגַן הַכֹּהֲנִים הָתָם, כֵּיוָן דְּאֶפְשָׁר – לָא טָרְחִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the quoted משנה supports רבה's comparison by naming the shared principle.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי ישמעאל's three סאה on שבת rests on the same idea as רבי חנינא's single reaper.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The principle כיון דאפשר לא טרחינן, found in רבי חנינא's ruling.

steps.title: Maybe רבי ישמעאל only says this where there is no publicity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה's comparison. Perhaps רבי ישמעאל reduces to three סאה only because five סאה adds no publicity. In the cutting case, more people do add publicity, so there he may agree with the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Perhaps רבי ישמעאל only says his ruling here, where nothing extra is publicized. But there, where using more people does publicize the event, say he holds like the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבה's link between רבי ישמעאל and רבי חנינא. It shows that the two cases might not be the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using five סאה instead of three is done privately, so cutting it down on שבת loses nothing public. Having three people cut the barley makes the מצוה more noticeable to everyone. So רבי ישמעאל could reduce effort in his own case and still require three cutters, like the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this? It opens a challenge to an assumption.
Perhaps. It offers another way to understand something.
He only said this in this specific case. His ruling may not carry over to other cases.
Publicizing the matter, making the מצוה well known

phrases.aramaic: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר
phrases.english: From where do you know this? Perhaps he only said it
Rabbi Yishmael, here,
phrases.notes: "Here" means his own case: bringing the עומר from three סאה instead of five.

phrases.english: because there is no publicizing of the matter,
but there, where there is publicizing of the matter,
phrases.notes: "There" is the cutting of the barley. More people cutting makes the event more public.

phrases.english: say that he holds like the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison that רבה made in steps 3-5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that רבי ישמעאל agrees with רבי חנינא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two cases differ in publicity. Extra cutters make the event public, but extra סאה do not.

steps.title: Maybe רבי חנינא only says this where the service is still done properly
steps.stepSummary: A second rejection, this time from רבי חנינא's side. With one cutter or three, the barley is still cut properly for the Temple. Using only three סאה makes the עומר less than its proper form, so רבי חנינא might agree with the רבנן there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively, רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים only said his ruling there. Whether one person cuts or three, the need of the Most High is done properly. But here, the need of the Most High is not done properly, so say he holds like the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second reason the comparison fails. This time it looks at רבי חנינא's case instead of רבי ישמעאל's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי חנינא's case, the number of cutters does not change the offering itself, which comes out complete either way. In רבי ישמעאל's case, three סאה instead of the usual five gives a lesser עומר. So רבי חנינא might allow less work only when the offering itself is not harmed.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively. It introduces a second, separate argument.
Deputy of the כהן גדול
The need of the Most High, meaning the Temple service
In its proper, complete manner

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי, עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר
phrases.english: Alternatively, he only said it
Rabbi Chanina, the deputy High Priest, there,
because whether with one or with three,
phrases.notes: Whether one person or three people do the cutting.

phrases.english: the need of the Most High is done properly,
but here, where it is not done
properly, the need of the Most High,
phrases.notes: Three סאה gives less than the normal five, so the עומר is not in its full form.

phrases.english: say that he holds like the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי, עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא סְגַן הַכֹּהֲנִים הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, separate reason to reject the same comparison.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that רבי חנינא would agree with רבי ישמעאל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Reducing the number of cutters does not harm the offering, but reducing the סאה does.

steps.title: רב אשי matches רבי ישמעאל with רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי sets aside the failed comparison. He says רבי ישמעאל and רבי יוסי hold the same view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: רבי ישמעאל and רבי יוסי said the same thing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a new partner for רבי ישמעאל's view. He is setting up the proof that comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows that the comparison to רבי חנינא has been dropped. Now רב אשי will point to a different case where a תנא also avoids extra work on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It drops an earlier approach and starts a new one.
They said the same thing, meaning they hold the same idea

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Yosei
said the same thing,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected comparison with a new one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל's view matches the view of רבי יוסי.

steps.title: The משנה about witnesses of the new moon
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says witnesses may break שבת to report the new moon, whether it was clearly seen or not. רבי יוסי says that if it was clearly seen, they may not break שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: Whether the new moon was seen clearly or not seen clearly, witnesses may break שבת for it. רבי יוסי says: If it was seen clearly, they may not break שבת for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings the משנה from ראש השנה that shows רבי יוסי's view. This is the source for his comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion lets witnesses travel on שבת to report the moon in every case. רבי יוסי says that if the moon was clearly seen by everyone, these witnesses should not travel. Others will surely report it anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: Clearly, plainly visible to everyone
They break שבת by doing a forbidden act, here traveling to testify
Whether... or. Both cases have the same ruling.

phrases.english: As we learned: whether it was seen clearly
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in ראש השנה (21b) about witnesses who saw the new moon.

phrases.english: or whether it was not seen clearly,
they may desecrate Shabbat for it.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אִם נִרְאָה בַּעֲלִיל –
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: If it was seen clearly,
they may not desecrate Shabbat for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: בֵּין שֶׁנִּרְאָה בַּעֲלִיל וּבֵין שֶׁלֹּא נִרְאָה בַּעֲלִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the משנה that backs up רב אשי's claim.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that רבי ישמעאל and רבי יוסי share one idea
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in ראש השנה about witnesses of the new moon

steps.title: The shared idea: if it can be done anyway, we don't add effort
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains the link. רבי יוסי says that since the moon will be reported anyway, we don't make extra effort on שבת. רבי ישמעאל says the same: since the עומר can come from three סאה, we don't make the effort for five.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't רבי יוסי say there: since it is possible, we don't make extra effort? Here too: since it is possible, we don't make extra effort.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the common idea behind רבי יוסי and רבי ישמעאל. This ties the proof together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, the court can get testimony from others, so these witnesses don't need to travel. For רבי ישמעאל, the עומר can be brought from three סאה, so we don't cut five on שבת. Both say that when the goal is reachable with less, we don't do extra work on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't he...? It introduces a point that is obvious from the source.
Since it is possible to manage without it
We don't go to extra trouble
Here too, the same applies

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי's proposal ties רבי ישמעאל's three-סאה rule to רבי יוסי through כיון דאפשר לא טרחינן. Steps 11 and 12 reject this comparison too.

phrases.aramaic: מִי לָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הָתָם,
phrases.english: Didn't Rabbi Yosei say there:
since it is possible, we don't go to extra trouble?
phrases.notes: He means it is possible to get the testimony from other witnesses who saw the moon too.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן דְּאֶפְשָׁר – לָא טָרְחִינַן.
phrases.english: Here too, since it is possible, we don't go to extra trouble.
phrases.notes: Here it is possible to bring the עומר from three סאה, so we don't cut five on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הָתָם, כֵּיוָן דְּאֶפְשָׁר לָא טָרְחִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה in step 9 matches רבי ישמעאל.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי ישמעאל and רבי יוסי share one principle
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי's reasoning in the new moon משנה: כיון דאפשר לא טרחינן

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל may agree with the Rabbis about the witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב אשי's comparison. רבי ישמעאל cuts back only for the עומר, where no future harm results. With the witnesses, sending some home could make them stop coming in the future, so there he may agree with the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Maybe רבי ישמעאל only says this about the עומר, where cutting back causes no future harm. With the witnesses, turning them away would make them stop coming later. So maybe there he agrees with the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב אשי. It says רבי ישמעאל might not agree with רבי יוסי after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the עומר, using three סאה instead of five hurts no one later. With the witnesses, if we tell some of them their trip was not needed, next time they may not bother coming, even when they are needed. So רבי ישמעאל could hold like the רבנן in the witness case.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do you know this?
He only said this in this case (and maybe not elsewhere)
You would cause them to stumble in the future (they won't come next time)
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: From where do you know this?
Perhaps he only says this
Rabbi Yishmael, here,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the עומר case, where he allows three סאה on שבת.

phrases.english: because there is no concern of
"you will cause them to stumble in the future,"
but there,
phrases.notes: "There" means the witnesses coming to report the new moon.

phrases.english: where you would cause them to stumble in the future,
say that he holds like the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אשי's link from step 10, from רבי ישמעאל's side.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רבי ישמעאל agrees with רבי יוסי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The witness case has a special worry: discouraged witnesses may stop coming. The עומר case has no such worry.

steps.title: רבי יוסי may agree with the Rabbis about the עומר
steps.stepSummary: A second rejection, from רבי יוסי's side. The new moon testimony is not a need of the Most High, so רבי יוסי limits breaking שבת. The עומר is a Temple need for which שבת is set aside, so he may agree with the רבנן there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else: רבי יוסי only says this about the witnesses, where there is no need of the Most High and שבת was not meant to be set aside. But the עומר is a need of the Most High, and שבת was meant to be set aside for it. So maybe there he agrees with the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another reason the comparison fails. This time it says רבי יוסי might not agree with רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עומר is an offering for the Temple, a צורך גבוה, and שבת is set aside for it. Reporting the new moon is not a Temple offering. So רבי יוסי may limit work on שבת only for the witnesses. For the עומר he may say to do it fully, like the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively; or else
A need of the Most High, something done for the Temple service
שבת was meant to be set aside for this

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי's link between רבי ישמעאל and רבי יוסי is rejected from both directions. Each one might agree with the רבנן in the other case.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי, עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר
phrases.english: Alternatively, he only says this
Rabbi Yosei, there,
because there is no need of the Most High,
and Shabbat was not meant to be set aside,
but here, where there is a need of the Most High,
phrases.notes: "Here" is the עומר, an offering brought in the Temple.

phrases.english: and Shabbat was meant to be set aside,
say that he holds like the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי, עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, parallel rejection of רב אשי's link, this time from רבי יוסי's side.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רבי יוסי agrees with רבי ישמעאל about the עומר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The עומר is a צורך גבוה for which שבת is set aside. The new moon testimony is not, so the cases are different.

steps.title: Slaughtering an extra communal sin offering on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A new topic. Someone slaughtered two חטאות ציבור on שבת when only one was needed. רבה (or רבי אמי) says he is liable for the second and exempt for the first. This is true even if the atonement came through the second, and even if the first turned out to be too thin.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: If someone slaughtered two communal sin offerings when only one was needed, רבה (some say רבי אמי) said he is liable for the second and exempt for the first. This holds even if the atonement came through the second one, and even if the first was found to be thin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new discussion about extra work on שבת. It brings a ruling about slaughtering one animal too many.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering the first animal was permitted on שבת, because one offering was needed. The second was extra, so slaughtering it broke שבת. The two "even if" cases make the rule stronger: we judge by the moment he slaughtered, when the first one already seemed to be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Communal sin offerings, brought for the whole people
Liable, here meaning he broke שבת
Exempt, not liable
Atonement was achieved
Thin or gaunt (a poor-quality animal)

steps.confusionAlert: "Liable" here is not about a problem with the offering itself. It means he broke שבת by slaughtering an animal that was not needed.

phrases.english: It was stated:
If one slaughtered two communal sin offerings,
and he needed only one.
Rabba said, and some say it was Rabbi Ami:
He is liable for the second,
and exempt for the first.
And even if atonement came through the second,
and even if the first was found to be thin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: שָׁחַט שְׁתֵּי חַטָּאוֹת שֶׁל צִיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion. It continues the theme of how much work may be done on שבת for Temple needs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering an extra communal offering on שבת makes him liable for the second animal and exempt for the first. This is true even if the second gave the atonement, or the first was found to be thin.

steps.title: רבה's other ruling about a fat animal and a thin one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that רבה said this even when the first animal was thin. In another ruling, רבה says that if he slaughtered the thin one first and then the fat one, he is exempt. In fact, we even tell him to bring the fat one and slaughter it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבה really say this? But רבה said: If he had two sin offerings, one fat and one thin, and he slaughtered the fat one and then the thin one, he is liable. If he slaughtered the thin one first and then the fat one, he is exempt. Not only that, we even tell him: bring the fat one from the start and slaughter it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבה can say this, since another ruling of his seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13, רבה said he is liable for the second animal even if the first was thin. Here רבה says that after a thin first animal, slaughtering the fat second one is exempt, and is even what he should do. These two rulings seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Did רבה really say this? (opens a challenge from his own words)
A fat, choice animal
Not only that, but even more
From the start; the proper way to act

phrases.english: And did Rabba really say this?
phrases.notes: "This" is the end of step 13: liable even if the first animal was thin.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabba say:
If there were two sin offerings before him,
one fat and one thin,

phrases.aramaic: שָׁחַט שְׁמֵינָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ שָׁחַט כְּחוּשָׁה – חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: if he slaughtered the fat one and then the thin one, he is liable;
the thin one and then the fat one, he is exempt;
and not only that, but we say to him:
Bring the fat one, from the start, and slaughter it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבָּה הָכִי? וְהָא אָמַר רַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the last "even if" clause of רבה's ruling in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The clause in step 13 saying he is liable for the second animal even when the first was thin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה elsewhere says a thin first animal makes slaughtering the fat second one exempt, and even proper. So he cannot also say the second one makes him liable.

steps.title: Two ways to fix the contradiction in רבה's rulings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives two answers. Either remove the words 'even if the first was thin' from רבה's first ruling, or say that the first ruling was really said by רבי אמי and not רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: take the case of the thin animal out of the first statement. Or if you want, say: that first statement was said by רבי אמי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from step 14 between two rulings of רבה. It offers two possible fixes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Answer one: רבה never said 'even if the first was thin,' so his two rulings no longer clash. Answer two: the first ruling belongs to רבי אמי, since step 13 already mentioned that some say it in his name. Two different sages are allowed to disagree, so there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say. Introduces one of several possible answers
Remove. Take these words out of the statement
Thin or weak (an animal of poor quality)

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
remove the 'thin' case from the first statement;
phrases.notes: He means: cross out 'even if the first turned out thin' from רבה's ruling back in step 13.

phrases.english: and if you wish, say:
that one was said by רבי אמי.
phrases.notes: Step 13 said the ruling came from רבה 'or רבי אמי.' Here we pick רבי אמי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: סְמִי כְּחוּשָׁה מִקַּמָּיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual correction or reassigning the ruling to a different sage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה said both rulings, and they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Either the 'thin' clause is removed, or the first ruling belongs to רבי אמי. Either way, רבה does not contradict himself.

steps.title: Do we judge by intention or by action?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי about a case where the first animal is later found to be weak in its innards. Do we go after the person's intention, which was to do an unneeded forbidden act, or after what actually happened, which turned out to be a needed act?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: If the first animal was found to be weak in its innards, what is the law? Do we go after his intention, and this man meant to do something forbidden? Or perhaps we go after his actions?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא asks a new question that builds on the case of the two חטאות. The first animal turns out to be flawed inside, but nobody knew this when the second one was slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he slaughtered the second animal, he thought it was not needed, so he meant to break שבת for nothing. In fact, the first animal was flawed, so the second was really needed. The question is which counts: his mind or the real result.

keyTerms.meaning: Innards, intestines
His intention, what he had in mind
His actions, what actually happened
He intended to do something forbidden

steps.whyThisMatters: The question of intention versus action is a basic issue across the laws of שבת and beyond.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
if the first animal was found to be weak in its innards,
what is the law?
Do we go after his intention,
and this man intended to do something forbidden,
or perhaps we go after his actions?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: נִמְצֵאת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה כְּחוּשָׁה בִּבְנֵי מֵעַיִין, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new question on the two-חטאות case from step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether liability on שבת depends on the person's intention or on the actual result, when the first animal turns out to be flawed.

steps.title: Comparing to the case of the drowning child
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי points to the dispute between רבה and רבא. A person heard that a child was drowning and spread a net to catch fish. If he caught only fish, he is liable. If he caught fish and the child, רבא says he is liable and רבה says he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Isn't this the case of רבה and רבא? As it was said: If one heard that a child was drowning in the sea, and he spread a net to bring up fish and brought up fish, he is liable. If he meant to bring up fish, and he brought up fish and the child, רבא says he is liable, and רבה says he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers by pointing to a known argument that looks similar. He sets up the comparison, which the next step will refine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the fish case, the man meant to do a forbidden act (catching fish), but his act also saved a life, which is allowed on שבת. רבא goes by his intention and makes him liable. רבה goes by the good result and exempts him. At first glance this looks just like רבינא's question.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't this the same as...?
A net or trap
A child
Liable / exempt

steps.confusionAlert: Saving a life on שבת is permitted, so the only question is whether his wrong intention (catching fish) still makes him liable.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Isn't this the case of Rabba and Rava?
As it was stated:
if one heard that a child was drowning in the sea,
and he spread a net to bring up fish
and he brought up fish, he is liable.
If he meant to bring up fish, and he brought up fish and the child:
Rava says: he is liable,
and Rabba says: he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו הַיְינוּ דְּרַבָּה וְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question by linking it to an existing dispute.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In this first version, רב אשי raises the רבה–רבא net dispute only to set it aside: as step 18 explains, רבה exempts only because the man heard about the child, so in the animal case everyone agrees he is liable.

steps.title: Even רבה agrees he is liable here
steps.stepSummary: רבה exempts only because the man heard about the child, so we assume he also had the child in mind. If he had not heard, even רבה would make him liable. In the animal case he never knew about the flaw, so everyone agrees he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה only exempts him there because he heard. We say that his mind was also on the child. But if he did not hear, he is not exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the comparison. It shows that רבה's lenient view does not apply to רבינא's case, so the person is liable according to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's exemption depends on the man knowing about the child, which lets us say he partly meant to save him. In the case of the two חטאות, nobody knew the first animal was flawed, so there was no good intention at all. That makes it like 'did not hear,' where both רבה and רבא agree he is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: He only exempts in this specific case
His mind, his intention
Since he heard (he knew)

steps.whatToRemember: If someone did a forbidden act on שבת with no idea it would turn out to be needed, he is liable according to everyone. רבה's exemption needs at least some awareness of the good purpose.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַד כָּאן רַבָּה לָא קָא פָּטַר
phrases.english: And Rabba only exempts him
because he heard,
so we say his mind was also on the child;
but if he did not hear, not.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד כָּאן רַבָּה לָא קָא פָּטַר אֶלָּא כֵּיוָן דְּשָׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the comparison from step 17 and decides רבינא's question.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: When the first animal's flaw was unknown, the person who slaughtered the second is liable according to both רבה and רבא.

steps.title: Second version: the dispute is about actions versus intention
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רב אשי tells רבינא that the animal case is the same as the dispute between רבה and רבא about the net. רבה follows a person's actions, and רבא follows his intention.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רב אשי answered: This is exactly the dispute between רבה and רבא. It was taught: A person heard that a child fell into the sea. He spread a net to bring up fish, and he brought up only fish. He is liable. If he meant to bring up fish and brought up both the child and fish, רבה says he is exempt and רבא says he is liable. רבה exempts because we follow his actions. רבא makes him liable because we follow his intention.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of רב אשי's answer to רבינא's question from Step 16. In this version, the net case shows a real general dispute that also decides the animal case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (Steps 17-18), רבה exempts only because the man heard about the child, so the animal case was liable according to everyone. Here, רבה exempts simply because the act turned out to be useful, even though the man did not mean it that way. So in the animal case, רבה would exempt and רבא would make him liable.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute between sages
A net or trap
Go after his actions, meaning judge by what actually happened
His intention or thought

steps.whatToRemember: In the second version, רבה follows actions and רבא follows intention. That makes the animal case a real dispute between them, not a case where everyone agrees.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In the first version, רבה exempts only because the man heard about the child. In this version, the reason has nothing to do with hearing. רבה always follows what actually happened.

phrases.english: And some say: he said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב אשי answering רבינא's question about the animal that turned out to be weak inside.

phrases.english: This is the dispute of רבה and רבא,
as it was stated:
If he heard that a child was drowning in the sea,
and he spread a net to bring up fish
and he brought up fish, he is liable.
If he meant to bring up fish and brought up the child and fish:

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה אָמַר: פָּטוּר, וְרָבָא אָמַר: חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: רבה says he is exempt, and רבא says he is liable.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה אָמַר פָּטוּר – זִיל בָּתַר מַעֲשָׂיו,
phrases.english: רבה says exempt, because we go after his actions,

phrases.aramaic: וְרָבָא אָמַר חַיָּיב – זִיל בָּתַר מַחְשַׁבְתּוֹ.
phrases.english: and רבא says liable, because we go after his intention.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַיְינוּ פְּלוּגְתַּיְיהוּ דְּרַבָּה וְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רב אשי's answer, in contrast to the conclusion of Step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Answers רבינא's question from Step 16: do we follow intention or outcome when the animal turns out to have been needed?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It depends on the dispute. רבה follows actions and would exempt. רבא follows intention and would make him liable.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to this version, the animal case is a dispute between רבה and רבא.

steps.title: Ten people pick figs for one sick person
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that if a sick person needs one fig on שבת and ten people each pick one, they are all exempt. This is true even if they picked one after another, and even if he was already healed by the first fig.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: A sick person was judged to need one dried fig. Ten people ran and brought ten figs at the same time. They are all exempt. This is true even if they came one after the other, and even if the sick person had already been healed by the first fig.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבה about extra work done on שבת to save a life. Everyone who rushed to help is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It might seem that only the first person's picking was needed, so the others did forbidden work for nothing. רבה says no: everyone who acted to save a life is exempt. That holds even if the sick person was already healed before the later ones arrived.

keyTerms.meaning: They judged or assessed him (the doctors decided what he needs)
A dried fig
At the same time
One after the other
He became healthy

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that people should not hold back from saving a life on שבת out of fear that someone else already did it. Everyone who rushes to help is exempt.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה: חוֹלֶה שֶׁאֲמָדוּהוּ לִגְרוֹגֶרֶת אַחַת,
phrases.english: רבה said: A sick person whom they judged to need one dried fig,
and ten people ran

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵבִיאוּ עֲשָׂרָה גְּרוֹגְרוֹת בְּבַת אַחַת – פְּטוּרִין,
phrases.english: and brought ten figs at the same time: they are exempt,
even if they came one after the other,
even if he had already been healed by the first one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: חוֹלֶה שֶׁאֲמָדוּהוּ לִגְרוֹגֶרֶת אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new ruling on the related theme of doing more forbidden work than needed to save a life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone who picks a fig for the sick person is exempt, even if they came one after another, and even after he was already healed.

steps.title: Two figs on two stems or three figs on one stem
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks: if a sick person needs two figs, should we pick two figs that hang on two separate stems, or three figs that hang on one stem, which means less picking?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: A sick person was judged to need two figs. There are two figs on two separate stems, and three figs on one stem. Which do we bring? Do we bring the two, because that is what he needs? Or perhaps we bring the three, because that means less picking?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a practical question. Should we bring exactly the amount the sick person needs, or the option that needs fewer acts of picking?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two figs on two stems means two separate acts of picking. Three figs on one stem means only one act of picking, but it gives him more fruit than he needs. The question is which matters more: the amount of fruit or the number of forbidden acts.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked, raising a question he was unsure about
Stem / stems that attach the fruit to the tree
Because they are fit for him (exactly what he needs)
Reaping or picking, one of the forbidden kinds of work on שבת

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי רָבָא: חוֹלֶה שֶׁאֲמָדוּהוּ לִשְׁתֵּי גְּרוֹגְרוֹת,
phrases.english: רבא asked: A sick person whom they judged to need two figs,
and there are two figs on two stems,
and three on one stem:
Which of them do we bring?
Do we bring two, because they are what he needs,

steps.title: Obviously we bring the three figs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it is obvious we bring the three figs on one stem.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious: we bring the three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer רבא's question. It says the answer is clear: bring the three figs, and the reasoning continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picking three figs on one stem is a single act of work. Picking two separate stems is two acts. So bringing three means doing less forbidden work, even though he gets more fruit than he needs.
